note: THE RECORD THAT DATES THE 1904 AVENUE. The Board's report of 2 November 1903 lists every street it had paved since the 1901 statute with an inspector's note, and it includes 'Prairie avenue from 16th street to 20th street. Good condition.--P. J. O'Donnell.' (p. 1390). So the asphalt the Council ordered on 9 February 1903 was down eight months before the scene date, and the same stretch is reported again, 'asphalt. R. F. Conway Co., contractor. In good condition', on 7 November 1906 (chicago_council_proceedings_1907_v58). Two records either side of 1 July 1904 name the same surface: it is ATTESTED for the scene. The list is also read for what it omits: no street or alley of the grid other than Prairie Avenue 16th-20th is in it, so the macadam of the cross streets and of Prairie Avenue 20th-22nd was not laid by the Board in 1901-03.
what_it_supplies: that Prairie Avenue from 16th to 20th Street had been paved (with the asphalt of the 9 February 1903 ordinance) and was in good condition on 2 November 1903
that no other street or alley of the 1904 grid was paved by the Board between 1901 and November 1903
